analysis.title: Marketcolour + HF Update / GS Macro Outlooks / SCA Dg / RHM Cut / B&M
key_insights: US equities fell on Friday amid a tougher risk backdrop: VIX at 20, 10-year yield at 5.13%, USD breaking out, oil above $90. SPX -40bp to 7561, NDX -91bp to 25136, RTY -31bp to 2790.
NDX broke a 4-week losing streak with semis +8% on the week but remains below its 200-day moving average. NVDA lost about $500bn of market cap while AMD and AVGO together added about $500bn or more.
Semis have underperformed the S&P by more than 30% since June, the sharpest relative drawdown since 2002. The GS AI Semis basket (GSCBSMHX) trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P.
Net selling in US Financials last week was the largest in 8 months (99th percentile over 5 years).
In Europe, EU Big Oils (GSXEBOIE) rose 1.9% and EU Luxury (GSXELUXG) fell 60bp after Richemont results (CFR SE -3.8%).

This week's catalysts: NVDA on Tuesday (first report under interim CEO Colette Kress), BABA on Thursday, and consumer prints (TSN, ARMK Mon; HD Tue; TJX, TGT, LOW Wed; WMT, ROST, GAP Thu; BJ Fri). Macro is lighter, with US Retail Sales on Tuesday and FOMC minutes on Wednesday.
Fundamental L/S hedge funds were up 1.1% last week (alpha -0.3%), with alpha losses from China equities and Health Care. YTD they are up 9.7% (alpha +7.1%).

HFs net sold US equities for a second straight week (5 of the last 6), driven by single-stock short sales and partly offset by short covers and long buys in macro products. US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.6 pts to 209.1% (34th percentile one-year) and net leverage rose 2.1 pts to 45.4% (4th percentile one-year).

The GS cash desk saw persistent NVDA supply from the long-only community, with money rotating into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech. Appetite to re-engage remains limited despite NDX snapping its losing streak.
Dom Wilson outlines 10 market themes for 2027, including a maturing cycle, AI impulse peaking, and bonds reclaiming macro and hedging value.

GS downgrades SCA to Sell as a high conviction call. Numbers are about 10% below the Street and downside to the price target is 16%. The call draws on work on global pulp supply and demand and on London Pulp Week.

GS cut Rheinmetall estimates after Q3 results and a fireside chat with the CEO, ahead of cuts likely at the upcoming CMD. 2030 EBIT falls 25% and EPS falls 30%, to about 104 for 2030. The largest cuts are in Weapons & Ammo, where growth momentum has deteriorated. Shares trade on under 8x 2030e P/E.

GS raised B&M to a 345p price target from 220p (Neutral), lifting FY27E/FY28E LFL to +2.3%/+3% (from +0.7%/+1%) and gross margin by +100bp/+30bp (from flat). FY27E/28E PBT rises 6%/15% to £310mn/£344mn.
CTA positioning in NDX is back near max short.

market_movers.rationale: SCA downgraded to Sell on estimates about 10% below the Street and 16% downside to the price target, based on work on global pulp supply and demand.
B&M target raised on higher FY27E/FY28E LFL and gross margin assumptions plus updated DCF inputs, lifting PBT estimates.
Rheinmetall 2030 EBIT cut 25% and EPS cut 30% to about 104 for 2030, led by Weapons & Ammo where growth momentum has weakened. Shares still trade below 8x 2030e P/E.

earnings_insights: NVDA reports Tuesday, its first report under interim CEO Colette Kress. Date and event only, no estimates given.
Rheinmetall Q3 results were reported and followed by GS estimate cuts: 2030 EBIT -25%, EPS -30%, GSe 2030 EPS about 104. Further cuts are expected at the CMD.
B&M estimates raised: FY27E/FY28E PBT +6%/+15% to £310mn/£344mn (GS estimates).
Richemont numbers reported Friday, with CFR SE down 3.8%.
Consumer earnings this week: TSN, ARMK Monday; HD Tuesday; TJX, TGT, LOW Wednesday; WMT, ROST, GAP Thursday; BJ Friday. BABA reports Thursday.
